```{r list-app, include=FALSE}
str0 <- ""

list_app <- function(nickname, dir_out_figtab, abcd, descr_short, descr_frag) {

  a <- list.files(path = dir_out_figtab, 
                  pattern = nickname, 
                  full.names = FALSE)
  
  nickname0 <- gsub(pattern = ".rdata",  
                    replacement = "", 
                    x = a[grepl(pattern = ".rdata", x = a)], 
                    ignore.case = TRUE)
  
  captions <- data.frame()
  for (i in 1:length(nickname0)) {
    a <- readtext(paste0(dir_out_figtab, nickname0[i], ".txt"))
    captions <- dplyr::bind_rows(
      captions, 
      data.frame(
        "id" = nickname0[i], 
        "capt" = a$text))
  }
    # # (APPENDIX) Appendix {-}
    str0 <- paste0(
    ifelse(abcd == "A", 
'

', 
'\\pagebreak

'),

'## Appendix ',abcd,': List of ', descr_short,' 

Appendix ',abcd, " ", descr_frag, '

**List of Tables**

',
text_list(paste0("\n\n - Appendix **", abcd, "** \\@ref(tab:", captions$id, "): ", captions$capt),
                 # sapply(list_tables00, #[grepl(x = names(list_tables00), pattern = "tab_app_taxa_encountered_")], "[[","header")), 
          sep = " ", sep_last = " ", sep_last2 = " "),
'

\\pagebreak

' )
    return(str0)
}

# https://support.authorea.com/en-us/article/how-to-create-an-appendix-section-or-supplementary-information-1g25i5a/
```

**Data Access**
 - Fisheries One Stop Shop public data portal^[https://www.fisheries.noaa.gov/foss]
 - Distribution Mapping and Analysis Portal^[https://apps-st.fisheries.noaa.gov/dismap/]
 - Alaska Fisheries Information Network^[https://apps-st.fisheries.noaa.gov/dismap/]

**General Resources**
 - Groundfish Assessment Program Bottom Trawl Surveys Landing Page^[https://www.fisheries.noaa.gov/alaska/science-data/groundfish-assessment-program-bottom-trawl-surveys]
 - AFSC’s Resource Assessment and Conservation Engineering Division^[https://www.fisheries.noaa.gov/about/resource-assessment-and-conservation-engineering-division]
 - Research Surveys conducted at AFSC^[https://www.fisheries.noaa.gov/alaska/ecosystems/alaska-fish-research-surveys]

**Latest Data Reports and Documents**
Data reports are also available for each of our historical surveys in the Gulf of Alaska, Aleutian Islands, eastern Bering Sea, northern Bering Sea, and Bering Sea slope through the publicly available NOAA Library^[https://repository.library.noaa.gov/]. The latest data reports are listed on our landing page (listed above). 

```{r app-social-media-latest-data-reports}
#| results: 'asis'
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false

source("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/afsc-gap-products/gap_products/refs/heads/main/content/references_current_tm.R") # srvy_cite 

# 1. Download the bib file to the code/ folder
bib_url <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/afsc-gap-products/gap_products/refs/heads/main/content/references.bib"
dest_file <- "code/references.bib"

# Create the code/ directory if it doesn't already exist
if (!dir.exists("code")) {
  dir.create("code", recursive = TRUE)
}

# Download the file
download.file(url = bib_url, destfile = dest_file, mode = "wb")

# 2. Read the local bib file
bib <- RefManageR::ReadBib(dest_file)

# 3. Extract unique citation keys from srvy_cite
cite_keys <- unique(srvy_cite$CITE)

# 4. Keep only keys that actually exist in the .bib file to prevent subsetting errors
valid_keys <- intersect(cite_keys, names(bib))

# 5. Subset the bibliography object
cite_subset <- bib[valid_keys]

# 6. Print directly with APA options, with no headers or separators
print(cite_subset, .opts = list(style = "markdown", 
                                bib.style = "authoryear", 
                                sorting = "none",
                                max.names = 99, 
                                dashed = FALSE))
```

Thank you to everyone who contributed your time, stories, photos, and expertise to make this season’s outreach possible. Your participation not only strengthens the Groundfish Assessment Program’s mission but also builds public understanding and appreciation of fisheries science.
We encourage you to explore, share, and continue contributing to these products.

## Appendix `r abcd`: Data Changes{#data-changes}

The `r maxyr` survey data products are generated by the *gapindex* R package (v`r packageVersion("gapindex")`)^[https://github.com/afsc-gap-products/gapindex] and distributed from tables stored in the AFSC GAP_PRODUCTS Oracle schema. These data are accompanied by extensive documentation, metadata, and user examples^[https://afsc-gap-products.github.io/gap_products/]. 

The AFSC Groundfish Assessment Program (GAP) team are stewards of the haul-level catch and effort data, as well as the catch per unit effort (CPUE), biomass, abundance, age composition, and size composition estimates. Improvements are made to these data and products as necessary and include fixing errors from past years, species vouchers, and incorporating new metadata. 
### Updates to individual historical records in data tables{#data-changes-updates}
Since the 2025 Bering Sea data report was published (June 2026; @EBS2025), there have been several updates to the GAP_PRODUCTS tables. Data in this report were updated as of `r last_production_run `.  Those changes are documented on our release notes page^[https://afsc-gap-products.github.io/gap_products/content/intro-news.html].
